title: Residence time drives an accelerating conversion gain across independent batches
core_conclusion: Increasing residence time raises conversion monotonically, the gain per hour itself grows with time, and this pattern reproduces across three independent batches rather than being carried by a single batch.

panels.role: trend + uncertainty — first-order main effect: conversion does rise with residence time
panels.claim: Batch conversion trajectories against residence time, with the pooled mean ± s.d. overlaid

panels.role: paired within-batch increment — rules out the claim being carried by a single batch
panels.claim: Per-hour increment for each batch, plotted at the interval midpoint

panels.role: distribution contrast — second-order claim: the per-hour gain itself grows, and that is not noise
panels.claim: Distribution of the per-hour increment for the 0–2 h and 3–5 h intervals
